title: Free Fall Force and Acceleration
learningObjectives: Calculate one-dimensional acceleration as net force divided by mass.
Describe free fall as motion with constant acceleration when gravity is the only external force.
Predict linear growth of velocity and quadratic growth of displacement under constant acceleration.

sources.title: Motion of Free Falling Object — NASA Glenn Research Center, Beginner's Guide to Aeronautics

evidence.quote: An object that falls through a vacuum is subjected to only one external force, the gravitational force, expressed as the weight of the object.
An object that is moving only because of the action of gravity is said to be free falling

explanations.text: Free fall is motion in a vacuum where the only external force is gravity, felt as weight.

evidence.quote: The acceleration is constant and equal to the gravitational acceleration g which is 9.8 meters per square second at sea level on the Earth.
The weight, size, and shape of the object are not a factor in describing a free fall.

explanations.text: Free-fall acceleration is constant at 9.8 meters per square second at sea level and does not depend on weight, size, or shape.

evidence.quote: Notice that the acceleration is a constant, the velocity increases linearly, and the location increases quadratically.
where a is the acceleration, V is the velocity, and X is the displacement from an initial location.

explanations.text: Under constant acceleration, velocity increases linearly with time while displacement from the start increases quadratically.

behavioralTests.name: negative net force gives negative acceleration
zero net force gives zero acceleration

predictions.prompt: A 2 kg object has a 19.6 N net force downward. What acceleration do you predict?
